explanation: No clear shared trigger. It fires on mixed tokens: '::' in C++ std::, whitespace or padding in code and config, broken non-Latin bytes, and function words in ordinary prose ('right to', 'research is'). It seems to like structural or space tokens inside technical text, but this does not predict well.

Function words (to, with, of, like, as, the) inside familiar fixed phrases, comparisons and idioms: 'as natural as seeing', 'like never before', 'Take Your Children to Work Day', 'in sync with', 'at the cost of', 'Friend of The Devil'. Prepositions in ordinary, non-idiomatic use fire weakly.

Words meaning something persists or continues despite pressure or expectation. It peaks on 'still' (a belief, problem or condition still holds) and also fires on cling, hold, remain, stays, stubborn and 'leave untouched'. Context about persistence boosts it.

Mixed: '::' namespace separators in Ruby and Rust, parts of numbers and citations (DOI digits, closing parentheses, slashes in year ranges), and scattered prose words ('receiver operating', 'answers yes to'). No single concept predicts it.

Polynomial definitions in generated math problems ('Let f(x) = ... x**[[2]] + ...'). It fires on the exponent digit of the x**2 or x**3 term, or on the '*x' / ' x' linear term. Outside such formulas it fires only weakly and sporadically, on code or text tokens.

Two unrelated jobs. (1) 'super' in method calls on the parent class ([super init...], super.viewDidLoad(), (Category)super.clone()). (2) Word pieces that finish a multi-token proper noun or technical word (Samo-an, Turkmen-istan, decom-pression, ser-pin, F-ij-ian, Sierra Leone).

The preposition or infinitive 'to' that follows a verb of using or taking plus its object and introduces the purpose or role: 'using this group as', 'used ... disclosures to', 'take it for', 'take ... into account', 'use the draft to', 'using django for'. It fires weakly elsewhere.

Code snippets in Q&A or programming text. It fires on the '=' of a variable assignment or declaration ('String url =', 'cursor =', 'self.name ='), and also on key ':' separators, indentation and declaration keywords (public, class, var) at the start of a code line.

Words that set up a group, set or collection: 'of' in 'list of', 'course of', 'string of'; collective nouns such as complex, team, bunch and network; quantity words such as several, plural and a number of; 'part of a larger'. Strongest on 'of' after a collection noun.

Mixed: URL path segments (/wiki, /master, www), the space or digit before the second number in a count ('91 malignant and 62', '19 men, 9 women'), digits in chemical formulas, and list or HTML tokens. Mostly predictable continuations in structured strings, but there is no single concept.

Verbs and nouns about supporting, defending or protecting a side or party: supporting, defend, side with, support, protect, protection, save, 'fight for'. It is strongest in political or military contexts. A minor offshoot fires on tokens in 'Solve ...' equations.

Mainly the decimal point or digit inside product, version or model numbers (Tab 7.0, 5.5-inch, Android Studio 2.3.3, WSO2 IS 5.7, BlackBerry Z10), and digits in years such as 'as of 2010'. It also fires on pieces of abbreviations and names (Att-ys, Madd-ow, Ad-aptable). Somewhat mixed.

Quantity and magnitude expressions: numbers and units in measurements (2 g/kg, 8f, $20 million, one-yard, 1 second, 11-year-old, six degrees, 220V, two-acre), plus size words (long, smaller, large, small). It fires on the token that gives the amount or unit.

Word pieces in the middle of foreign or transliterated proper names and non-English words (Greek, Russian place names, Finnish, Iranian romanizations, Japanese katakana, Polish surnames). It fires on fragments that are not complete English words. Digits inside long numbers fire moderately.
